4. Defendant 1-3 contested the suit by filing a written statement. Their case is that the land of the entire suit khatian being 47 was sold in auction in Rent Execution case 1495 of 1945. It was purchased by the original Zamindars and after keeping it in their possession for more than 2 years. The disputed land was settled to the defendants in 1358 B.S. and 1360 B.S. by the Zaminders on the basis of pattas. Defendants since then are in possession. Defendants denied the story of dispossession of the plaintiffs by them. 

 6. Plaintiff took, appeal, appellate court also found that since the original proceeding which was started for alleged sale in auction, namely, rent suit wherein the suit plot is not there. Therefore, auction sale and delivery of possession etc. all were manufactured and as such no title could be found in favour of the Zamindars who claimed to have purchased the suit land in the auction sale. Consequently. the defendants who claimed to have taken settlement on the basis of pattas from the Zamindars in the years 1358 and 1360. B.S. also cannot claim any title or their possession cannot be adverse in the suit land. Claim of title by adverse possession before the trial court was the anchor sheet of the case of the defendants. Appellate court has discussed the evidence to the fullest extent in respect of possession of the defendants relating to their documents namely, khatian, proceedings of rent suit, rent execution case, sale certificate and letter of delivery of possession etc. Appellate court found that onus was upon the defendants to prove their title by adverse possession as their claim of title on the basis of settlement from the zamindars through the pattas, failed, but the defendants according to the appellate court could not prove the same. 

 8. It is also found by the appellate court that in the rent suit and rent decree and the sale certificate proceeding etc. said Badruddin the predecessor interest of the plaintiffs had not been made party although he had purchased the suit land in 1929 from original Tenants of the suit land, namely Kheru and Yousuf and the suit plot was not subject matter of the rent suit and therefore plaintiff's title was not effected in any manner by the rent suit and the auction sale, sale certificate and by the so called letter of delivery of possession. Appellate court also after vivid discussion of the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same of the fullest extent has found that D.W.1 himself admitted that before him, Badruddin was in possession. Therefore, it has been correctly found by the appellate court that Badruddin was in possession. The property devolved upon the plaintiff after death of Badruddin. It also could be established by the plaintiffs that they were dispossessed from the suit land after the institution of the suit. It is not denied that Kheru and Yousuf were the original owners. So far the question of adverse possession is concerned which is the only basis of the defendant's claim, after concurrent finding of the courts below, that the defendants claim on the basis of auction purchase, in the rent execution by their Predecessors, the Zamindary and settlement from them to the defendants by patta etc. have failed, in any view of the dispute and in view of the appellate court's finding that the defendants could not establish their title by adverse possession the finding and decision of the trial court, as involved illegally Adverse possession must be hostile, notorious, continuous uniterrupted and actual. These elements are absent from the evidences of the defendants and the allegation of adverse possession is not caused by decision (See 1 PLR (Dhaka) P-395) of it, Defendants case of adverse possession fails as the defendants witness D.W. 1 himself admits plaintiffs possession, before their claim of adverse possession, as found by the appellate court as the last and final court of facts plaintiffs rather successfully proved their continuous possession in suit land title their dispossession.
